newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK journalists urge China not to curb press freedom.
newsitem.headline: HK journalists urge China not to curb press freedom.

text.p: More than 500 journalists in Hong Kong marked world press freedom day on Saturday, urging China and the territory's government-in-waiting not to curb press freedom after the handover.

The group, which included journalism tutors and students, took a half page advertisement in the mass-selling Apple Daily calling on Beijing and Hong Kong's future leader, Tung Chee-hwa, to adhere to the International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights after China resumes sovereignty on July 1.

They expressed concerns that the post-colonial government would legislate laws to curtail press freedom in the wake of Tung's plans to tighten laws covering civil and political liberties after the handover.
Pro-democracy activists in Hong Kong have strongly criticised the planned changes, which would limit the right to demonstrate and ban foreign donations to local political groups.
The British territory of Hong Kong reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30 after 156 years of colonial rule.
